items.title: 4 Overlooked Tech Stocks That Pay Dividends and Have Room to Grow
items.summary: Tech usually means buybacks and growth stories, not dividend checks. Four NASDAQ names, from an internet registry to a chip equipment giant, are about to pay out while barely touching their cash, and one carries a hidden catch.

items.title: Micron Soars 5% as TSMC Sticks to the “Global Logic IC” Industry, Not Memory
items.summary: Key TakeawaysMicron shares jumped 5% today after TSMC said it remains focused on logic chips, as Applied Materials and other chip stocks rebounded. TSMC staying out of memory removes Micron’s newest supply worry, though China’s CXMT is still pushing into server memory.

items.summary: Key TakeawaysMunro Partners, a fund with $4. 4 billion in US stocks, made Applied Materials (AMAT:NASDAQ), Alphabet (GOOGL:NASDAQ) and Quanta Services (PWR:NYSE) its three biggest new or added positions in the quarter ended June 30.

items.title: Cathie Wood and 73 Other Funds Bought Chip Stocks. Cerebras Is Down 59% Since. Time to Buy?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysCathie Wood’s ARK and dozens of other funds held Cerebras (CBRS:NASDAQ), Intel (INTC:NASDAQ), KLA (KLAC:NASDAQ), Applied Materials (AMAT:NASDAQ), or Lam Research (LRCX:NASDAQ) as of June 30, and all five stocks have fallen 53% to 59% since. Cerebras was a new holding for every fund that owned it.

items.title: Applied Materials (AMAT) Stock Looks Above Fair Value After Its 127% Run
items.summary: Applied Materials has ridden the AI chip equipment wave to strong longer term gains, yet the recent pullback now puts a sharper spotlight on whether the current price still lines up with the cash the business can generate over time. Over the past 3 years the stock has returned 127.5%, which puts a lot of past optimism into the valuation question around its future cash flows.
